newsitem.title: GERMANY: Frankfurt/Paris airports back air-rail link study.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt/Paris airports back air-rail link study.

text.p: Frankfurt and Paris airports as well as Deutsche Lufthansa AG, Air France and the German and French railways said they have launched an intermodal passenger transport research project.

The European project will focus on improving door-to-door baggage transport and better travel information for passengers going to airports by public transport, the organisations said at a joint news conference in Frankfurt.
Flughafen Frankfurt Main AG (FAG) said it will manage the two-year Ecu2.3 million European Passenger Traveller Care Services (EuroTraCS) project, which is half-funded by the European Union.

FAG Deputy Chairman Manfred Schoelch said: "We are convinced that the construction of railway lines and airport train stations needs to be supplemented by the integration of services supplied by carriers independently of one another."
Only about 10 percent of Frankfurt airport's 20 million local passengers arrived by train at present but FAG wanted to increase this to 30 percent, or 10 million, by 2010, he added.
The new German high-speed ICE railway station due to open in 1999 would include passenger and baggage airline check-in facilities, Schoelch said.
Anne Reinhardt-Lehmann, FAG marketing director, said passengers travelling to airports faced uncoordinated public transport and complicated pre-travel information.
The EuroTraCS project would carry out market research on customer needs and then launch pilot projects from 1998, she added. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
